Talk to the…

A recorder for long semi-structured interviews. It records once, straight through, while you navigate the questions — then hands you the recording and a timeline of everything you marked along the way.

  • ●Nothing leaves this device. There is no server behind this page. The recording and the notes stay in your browser until you save them.
  • ●One file, not one per question. A conversation that stops and starts is not a conversation. What you say between questions is kept too.
  • ●It works offline. Load this page once and you can run an interview with the network off.
  • ●In the room or on a call. On a video call it records the call audio alongside your microphone, so both halves are captured.
Sound — get this right before you start

Test the microphone every time, even one you used yesterday. A connected headset with a flat battery looks identical to a working one: it appears in the list, the browser grants it, and the level is zero. The consent screen has a sound check — talk at the distance you will actually sit and watch the needle clear the mark.

Pick the device by name, not by luck. The first time, the browser hides device names until you allow the microphone once; press Show me the device names and they appear. Choosing "whatever this computer is set to" is fine when you know what that is, and a trap when you do not.

If it dies mid-interview, change it — the recording keeps running. There is a microphone button beside the level meter. Switching does not stop or split the recording, and the change is marked on the timeline.

On a video call, a plain microphone records YOU and not them. Their voice comes out of your speakers, and the call software is actively removing that from your mic as echo. Choose Video call as the setting and share the call tab with audio when asked, or use a device that mixes both — a Farm Hack box can present one.

Wired beats Bluetooth for the recording that matters. A Bluetooth headset with its microphone open drops into narrowband mono, and this file is the source of the transcript and every quote that follows it.

Silence what interrupts. Notifications land in the recording, and a mix device captures everything you hear.

Running the interview

Read the consent aloud. It will not let you start until you confirm you did. What it says about where the recording goes is what the participant agreed to — if the recording later travels some other way, that is a thing to record, not to skip.

It records once, straight through. Not one file per question. What is said between questions is kept, which is usually where the interview actually happens.

The questions are a map, not a script. One is shown at a time with the next in view. Move when the conversation moves; skip freely. Pressing next marks the moment, and that mark is what lets a ninety-minute recording be read back question by question.

Write what they said as they say it. The box under the question is for their answer in your shorthand — it survives even if the audio never gets transcribed. The private note beside it is for your remark about the question, and the two are kept apart on purpose.

Flag the moments you will want again. The flag button stamps the time. Finding a quote afterwards is the difference between a flag and an afternoon.

Rate the questions. A question that fell flat is worth saying so about — that feedback is what the next version of the set is built from.

Ending. End interview is in the bar that never scrolls away. Give it a headline you would recognise in a list a year from now, then save — or send it to a box if someone gave you an address and a code.

Reviewing the questions

Every set below has a Review or comment on these questions link. Sets marked draft have not been reviewed by anyone yet and say so — those are the ones most worth your time before they are used with a real participant.

Review is not a formality here. Feedback against a version is what the next version is built from: a set cannot be forked without saying what changed and which feedback it answers, so a comment you leave is the thing a curator has to respond to.

The review page is served by a Farm Hack box. If you opened this page from a box, the links go straight there. If you are reading a copy hosted anywhere else, the first link you press will ask for a box address and then remember it.

The question sets in this page are public, versioned artifacts from the Farm Hack question-sets library. The answers are not: questions federate, answers do not.

Saving gives you two files — the recording, and a sidecar holding consent, your marks and your notes. Any Farm Hack box can ingest the pair as they are, and transcribe them locally. Built 2026-09-21 from question-set snapshot 2026-09-21, library 06a3dc4 + uncommitted changes.

Send it to a box

Question feedback is not sensitive, so most boxes take it without a code. If yours refuses, ask whoever runs it for a one-time code — the same kind an interview uses, issued from Listening & Research → Upload Codes.

Before we record

This interview runs

Read this aloud: I would like to record our conversation so I do not have to rely on my notes. The recording stays on this device and then on our own Farm Hack boxes — ours here, and the machine we use to turn speech into text. It does not go to any outside company. We keep a backup copy, and you can say where. You can ask me to stop at any point, ask for something to be struck from the record afterwards, and decide separately whether you are quoted by name.
